chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“It is not proper for a Muslim woman to wear, from khimārs and garments, that which does not cover anything.”

key_terms.الدُّرُوعِ: garments or dresses worn to cover the body
key_terms.الْخُمُرِ: head-coverings or veils worn by women
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; the female subject addressed in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمَةِ: the Muslim woman; indicating the ruling applies to believing women

ai.seo_question: What kind of clothing is not suitable for a Muslim woman to wear in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a Muslim woman's clothing in the context of salat (prayer). It states that head-coverings and garments must provide actual covering, and that clothing which does not conceal the body is not suitable.
